A guest submitted as 'User@Example.com' when the attendee row stores 'user@example.com' passes the dedupe and gets created as a duplicate attendee. The mechanism is visible in the diff; it's a minor correctness edge case rather than a misread.

judged_text: Case-sensitive existing-attendee dedupe: `guest === attendee.email` comparison doesn't lowercase the guest email, allowing case-variant duplicates of already-registered attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:68-76)

record.issue_text: Case-sensitive existing-attendee dedupe: `guest === attendee.email` comparison doesn't lowercase the guest email, allowing case-variant duplicates of already-registered attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:68-76)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with a case-sensitive comparison against existing attendees: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since the input schema only validates format (`z.string().email()`) and does not normalize casing, a guest like `Test@ex.com` can bypass the dedupe when an existing attendee email is `test@ex.com`, resulting in duplicate attendees being created via `createMany` and potentially duplicate notifications/calendar updates.
